paper.title_en: Molecular-orbital origin of weak orbital ferromagnetism and anomalous Hall effect in a trimerized kagome antiferromagnet
paper.abstract_en: We reveal the molecular-orbital origin of weak orbital ferromagnetism and the anomalous Hall effect (AHE) induced by noncollinear spin order in a trimerized kagome lattice. By transforming to the molecular-orbital basis of an isolated trimer in the double-exchange regime, we derive an effective low-energy model for the states with opposite orbital angular momenta $m= \pm 1$ subject to an effective Zeeman field arising from spin chirality and spin-orbit (SO) coupling. In this representation, the kagome-lattice problem maps onto a triangular lattice of trimers, while the nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor hoppings of the original lattice generate complex hopping amplitudes between neighboring trimers. This formulation provides a transparent picture of how spin chirality and SO coupling can be recast as an effective Zeeman field that lifts the degeneracy of the $m= \pm 1$ states, breaks time-reversal symmetry, and thereby gives rise to weak orbital ferromagnetism and the AHE. The resulting phase diagram includes metallic phases, topologically trivial insulating phases, as well as several topological phases characterized by nonzero Chern numbers and the quantum anomalous Hall effect. We further identify an alternative route to time-reversal-symmetry breaking and orbital magnetization, driven by an emergent gauge field arising solely from complex inter-trimer hoppings and requiring no effective Zeeman field.
